`apps/learn` has native TanStack Start + Vite+ + Void source beside its Next build,
generated by the [start-bridge codemod](/build/devops/start-bridge-codemod). Capture
the serving deployment for each URL before activation.

## Worker

- `apps/learn/void.config.ts` names the staging candidate (`workers_dev` on, `TUTURUUU_NOINDEX=1`). The production archive targets `tuturuuu-learn` with `workers_dev` and `preview_urls` off, `TUTURUUU_NOINDEX=0` and no configured routes; its custom domain and zone routes are managed in the provider, so a deploy leaves them in place.
- Entry: `apps/learn/cloudflare/worker.ts`; Wrangler config is emitted by `void` into `dist`.
- Root host: `learn.tuturuuu.com` (compiled in `start-bridge.config.ts` or the generated default).
- Mount: `tuturuuu.com/learn` (base path `/learn`), served by the same Worker
  (see [the mount](#tuturuuucomlearn-mount)).
- Binding: `ASSETS` (static output, `run_worker_first`).
- Variables (names): `TUTURUUU_NOINDEX`, optional `INTERNAL_WEB_API_ORIGIN` (default `https://tuturuuu.com`).
- Secrets (names, set in the Worker, never in the repo): `NEXT_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_URL`,
  `NEXT_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_PUBLISHABLE_KEY`, `SUPABASE_SECRET_KEY`,
  `TUTURUUU_APP_COORDINATION_SECRET` (see
  [App coordination secret rollout](/build/devops/app-coordination-secret-rollout)).
- Optional: `TUTURUUU_DEVBOX_CONTROL_URL` and `TUTURUUU_DEVBOX_CONTROL_TOKEN`.
  Without them the devbox wake signal is skipped and runners pick work up by
  polling (`packages/utils/src/devbox-control.ts`). The token is the
  `DEVBOX_CONTROL_INTERNAL_TOKEN` of `tuturuuu-devbox-control`, a single shared
  value: issuing a new one rotates it and revokes every existing copy.

## Document script policy

The Learn Worker enforces a fresh request nonce with `strict-dynamic` on both
`learn.tuturuuu.com` and `tuturuuu.com/learn`. The full document policy, including
Trusted Types, is report-only. Theme and Sorbet prepaint scripts receive the
request nonce during server rendering; client rendering omits it. The router
and bridge head scripts use the same request context. Regression coverage lives
in `apps/learn/start-bridge.config.test.ts` and the client-provider SSR and
hydration tests.

Runtime qualification requires the owning CI build and its package outputs.
A fresh source-only worktree can fail module resolution before serving a request;
that failure does not establish the root or mounted route's HTTP status. Preserve
the expected `200` assertions and qualify the emitted Worker in CI.

## Build and qualification

```bash
bun turbo:local run build --filter=@tuturuuu/learn^... --concurrency=2
bun scripts/ci/generate-build-metadata.ts
bun run --cwd apps/learn routes:check
bun run --cwd apps/learn type-check:cloudflare
bun run --cwd apps/learn build:cloudflare
CI=true CI_SOURCE_SHA=$(git rev-parse HEAD) bun run --cwd apps/learn test:runtime
```

`learn-cloudflare.yaml` runs the same steps in CI. The cutover job also runs the
emitted production Worker in workerd, seals the tested bytes and repeats the
cutover probes after restoring the archive in a clean checkout. Both URL variants
must render the landing page with a bare-path query, serve its emitted assets,
and preserve the full parent-invite destination through the Web login and
verification redirects. The mounted Worker rejects attempts to mint an app
session. Runtime credentials and outbound API responses use fixtures.

The same cutover suite checks the Learn side of the nested `tuturuuu.com/lms/learn`
mount on the candidate bytes (`cloudflare/lms-mount-acceptance.mjs`). A signed-out
registered nested page, with an encoded segment and repeated query, redirects to
the mounted login, which hands Web a `/verify-token` return URL naming the same
`/lms/learn` path. A localized link drops its locale inside the mount, and the
dashboard entry requires sign-in. A well-formed app session token with the wrong
signature redirects to login without outbound requests. The sampled responses
never set or clear a per-app session cookie, both minting endpoints answer `409`,
and the landing declares its apex canonical. The Worker answers `404` without
outbound requests for `/lms`, `/lms/teach` and look-alike prefixes. These checks
do not run Web's return flow, switch areas, or load the deployed `LEARN` binding;
hosted acceptance covers those with approved identities.

## Private smoke and route watch

```bash
curl -sI https://learn.tuturuuu.com/api/build-info      # 200, JSON, no-store
curl -sI https://learn.tuturuuu.com/                    # entry route, see below
curl -sI https://learn.tuturuuu.com/login               # renders, no 5xx
curl -sI https://learn.tuturuuu.com/robots.txt          # 200
curl -sI 'https://tuturuuu.com/learn?x=1&x=2'            # landing page
curl -sI https://tuturuuu.com/learn/api/build-info       # same commit as the subdomain
```

Before routing, upload the sealed bytes at zero traffic and run the same checks
against the pinned version. With an approved smoke identity, open a course and a
parent-invite fixture, read the timetable, save and remove a disposable progress
record, and verify an API call that falls through to Web. Repeat on both URL
variants. After activation, watch errors, redirects, asset status and sign-in for
30–60 minutes and roll back immediately on regression.

## tuturuuu.com/learn mount

- Zone routes `tuturuuu.com/learn` and `tuturuuu.com/learn/*` on `tuturuuu-learn`
  serve the bare path and every nested path, including `/learn/assets/*` and
  `/learn/api/*`. `/learning` and every other path stay on the gateway.
- A zone route cannot match the bare path once a query string is present, so
  the gateway also mounts `/learn`: `GATEWAY_MOUNTED_PATHS` lists `/learn` and
  `MOUNT_LEARN` binds `tuturuuu-learn` (see
  [Gateway Worker](/build/devops/gateway-worker#apps-mounted-at-tuturuuucomapp)).
  `apps/gateway/wrangler.jsonc` commits both, so a gateway deploy keeps them.
- Smoke: `curl -s https://tuturuuu.com/learn/api/build-info` returns the Learn
  build identity, and `https://tuturuuu.com/learn` and
  `https://tuturuuu.com/learn?x=1` render the Learn portal.

## Rollback

1. Cloudflare is the only production target; rollback never moves DNS or
   routes back to Vercel. Before each change, record the serving
   `tuturuuu-learn` version and, for a mount change, the serving
   `tuturuuu-gateway` version.
2. Code regression: roll `tuturuuu-learn` back to its recorded previous version
   (`cf` Worker version rollback, or a deployment at 100% of that version).
   Keep the custom domain, zone routes and gateway mount in place.
3. Mount regression: deploy the recorded previous `tuturuuu-gateway` version.
   `apps/gateway/wrangler.jsonc` commits the `/learn` mount and CI deploys merge
   it back, so hold gateway deploys until the fix lands (see
   [Gateway Worker](/build/devops/gateway-worker)).
4. Rerun the smoke checks against the Worker hosts and fix forward on Cloudflare.

Rolling back touches no database rows and no migrations. Route, DNS and deployment
changes belong to the release owner.

## Latency qualification

Compare cold starts and warmed requests separately for the same route mix.
The Worker serves fingerprinted Vite assets with immutable caching. HTML,
auth redirects and signed-in API responses keep their private cache policy.
The two dashboard menus and staff version badge share one profile load per
Start request. Dashboard bootstrap reads use the request’s verified identity
and coalesce repeat reads within the request, per API origin. Session assurance
finishes before the protected render starts. Include public landing, signed-in
workspace and static asset requests in the hosted watch.
Compare early and late windows with upstream status and rate-limit counts.
